subject: Armstrong to Madison, 20 February 1808: is any other letter in this cipher known?
body:
Dear Papers of James Madison team,

One person directs this project and sends this message; the reading, the searches of the editions and the audits are done by AI agents (Claude models) working in an open repository, every step logged. We work, with S. Tomokiyo's encouragement, on John Armstrong's cipher letter to James Madison of 20 February 1808 (Founders Online 99-01-02-2728; NARA RG 59, M34 roll 14, frames 0030-0033). We have not read it, and write to ask one question and pass on what we have ruled out.

The question: do you know of any other letter in this cipher, or carrying the same shorthand-like marks among the numbers -- in Armstrong's papers, or in the papers of the correspondent Madison meant when he wrote to Jefferson on 15 May 1808 that the cipher "must be one concerted with another correspondent"? With 369 number groups, over a third occurring only once, the letter cannot be read from its own text; a second letter in the same code is the single thing most likely to open it.

What we have checked, with the numbers on file in the repository linked below: a fresh transcription from the manuscript images; that the office codes Armstrong and Monroe used with Madison do not fit it; that six other coded Armstrong letters of 1806-1808 screen as their own code, not as this one; that Livingston's letters to Madison and the Armstrong-Jefferson letters are in clear; and that the marks among the numbers match none of ten period English shorthand systems.

If you know of such a letter, a key, a later decipherment, or who the "other correspondent" was, we would be very grateful for a pointer. Everything we have, including the negatives, is open at https://github.com/NoAutopilot/cipher-lab/tree/main/ciphers/armstrong-madison-1808 .

[SIGN-OFF]
notes: Question only, no reading claimed; gate 1 waived per ASKS row 66 (a question, not a claim). Address jmadison@virginia.edu verified today (26 Sept 2026, both at 13:43 UTC by the lane orchestrator and re-read by this worker) on https://pjm.as.virginia.edu/contact -- stable, no change. Folder and HYPOTHESES.md links included.
